ai-at-work.title: Ford rehires ‘gray beard’ engineers after AI falls short
ai-at-work.excerpt: "Mistakenly we thought that by just introducing artificial intelligence ... that would produce a high-quality product.”
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Ford brought back experienced engineers after discovering their AI-driven design process couldn't actually deliver a viable vehicle without human expertise. This matters because it's a real-world reminder that digital workplace tools, including AI, work best alongside experienced people, not instead of them. After three decades watching tech solve problems, I can tell you this headline should read "Ford Remembers How Products Actually Get Made" because no algorithm has ever replaced judgment, and apparently that's still a lesson Silicon Valley needs to keep learning.

ai-at-work.title: Don’t surrender data control in pursuit of intelligence
ai-at-work.excerpt: With organizations reorganizing themselves to put artificial intelligence at the center, we’ve seen a shift from information being valuable to being a means of achieving intelligence, which is far mor
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Organizations are increasingly handing over control of their data to AI and cloud vendors while chasing the promise of intelligence gains. For digital workplace pros, this matters because uncontrolled data sprawl creates security risks, compliance headaches, and vendor lock-in that nobody wants to untangle later. Here's the truth: you can have intelligent systems and keep your data safe, but it requires actual governance instead of just signing contracts and hoping for the best.

ai-at-work.title: Geopolitical tension highlights the need for risk intelligence
ai-at-work.excerpt: Within hours of the first U.S.-Israel strikes against Iran in February 2026, hacktivists went to work launching massive distributed denial-of-service attacks. Both pro- and anti-Iranian groups targete
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Geopolitical conflicts are now triggering coordinated cyberattacks within hours, with hacktivists targeting critical infrastructure across multiple sectors including telecoms, energy, and government systems. Digital workplace pros need to understand that your organization's security posture isn't just an IT checkbox anymore, it's a business continuity issue that can crater operations faster than a bad all-hands meeting. The real kicker is that most companies still treat geopolitical risk like weather forecasting, assuming it won't happen to them until it does.

ai-at-work.title: Unconventional AI debuts oscillator-based Un-0 model series
ai-at-work.excerpt: Unconventional AI Inc. has developed an artificial intelligence architecture that could improve the power efficiency of image generation models. The technology is the basis of a new neural network ser
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Unconventional AI just dropped a new neural network series called Un-1 that's supposed to run image generation models way more efficiently than current approaches. For those of us building digital workplace tools, this matters because lighter AI models mean faster performance and lower infrastructure costs when we're trying to embed AI into collaboration platforms without melting our servers. Honestly though, we'll believe the efficiency gains when we see them in production, not in a press release.

industry-news.title: AI Upgrades, Security Breaches, and Industry Shakeups Define the Week in Tech
industry-news.excerpt: See what you missed in Daily Tech Insider from June 22–26. The post AI Upgrades, Security Breaches, and Industry Shakeups Define the Week in Tech appeared first on TechRepublic.
industry-news.dwp_take: Another week where AI upgrades and security breaches are apparently competing for top billing like they're on some kind of twisted tech reality show. This matters because your workplace tools are getting smarter while simultaneously proving they're about as secure as a screen door on a submarine, which means IT teams need to actually think about what they're adopting instead of just chasing the shiny new thing. Here's the real talk: you can have all the AI features in the world, but if bad actors are walking through your front door, your productivity gains mean nothing.

industry-news.title: Microsoft Extends Windows 10 Security Updates to 2027
industry-news.excerpt: Microsoft extended Windows 10 security updates for personal devices through Oct. 12, 2027, giving users more time to upgrade. The post Microsoft Extends Windows 10 Security Updates to 2027 appeared fi
industry-news.dwp_take: Microsoft just kicked the Windows 10 retirement date down the road to October 2027, which means millions of people can keep using it on their personal devices without losing security patches. This matters because workplace IT teams have been sweating bullets trying to manage the chaos of mass Windows 11 migrations, and this extension gives them breathing room to plan upgrades more strategically instead of dealing with a panic-driven stampede. Honestly, this feels like Microsoft finally admitting that forcing everyone onto Windows 11 at once was about as realistic as getting your entire company to adopt a new collaboration tool in thirty days.

industry-news.title: AWS says cloud market gatekeeper designation risks ‘deterring European investment and innovation’ as EU regulators plot competition crackdown
industry-news.excerpt: Gatekeeper designation under the legislation would force AWS and Microsoft to make concessions
industry-news.dwp_take: AWS is pushing back against the EU's plan to designate them as a "gatekeeper" under new competition rules that would require major concessions to smaller competitors. For digital workplace pros, this matters because AWS and Microsoft cloud services underpin most enterprise infrastructure, and regulatory requirements could mean new compliance headaches, service changes, or pricing shifts you'll need to manage. Here's the thing: AWS framing this as a threat to innovation while simultaneously fighting transparency requirements is peak tech industry logic, like complaining a speed limit kills the joy of driving.

industry-news.title: Nationwide targets private cloud gains with VMware Cloud Foundation deal
industry-news.excerpt: The expanded collaboration will establish a unified private cloud platform for the high street lender
industry-news.dwp_take: Nationwide Building Society signed a deal to build a unified private cloud platform using VMware Cloud Foundation, aiming to modernize their infrastructure and reduce vendor sprawl. This matters because financial services organizations still run vast legacy systems, and consolidating cloud infrastructure is one of the few ways they can actually move faster without blowing up their operations. That said, I've seen "unified platforms" promised before, and Nationwide's success will depend entirely on whether they treat this as a technical project or finally admit it's actually a change management nightmare.
